analysis.title: Equities - Tactical Top Picks (2 Nov 2026)
key_insights: UBS lists 10 open tactical top picks as of 2 Nov 2026, all rated Buy. Seven also carry the CIO Most Preferred (MP) tag: Rolls-Royce, Siemens, Barclays, Oracle, Boeing, Johnson Controls and Orica. Oracle is the only new idea, added 2 Nov 2026.

Open ideas are mostly underwater since inception: Barclays -13.3%, Boeing -11.0%, Rolls-Royce -6.9%, Johnson Controls -5.0%, Rockwool -4.1%, Siemens -3.7%. Only Expeditors (+5.6%), Straumann (+4.7%) and Orica (+0.6%) are positive. Oracle has no performance figure yet.

Closed-idea record since inception: 272 ideas, average absolute performance 1.2% and relative 0.2%, with an average life of 38 trading days. Calendar 2026 YTD averages by region: Switzerland +6.8% absolute (+3.4% relative), Europe -0.4% (-1.6%), Americas -0.7% (-2.0%), Asia-Pacific -6.2% (-4.1%). 2025 averages were +0.5%, +2.7%, -1.2% and +2.8% absolute in the same order.

Straumann (Buy, PT CHF 115, price CHF 97.42): UBS sees consensus as achievable with modest room for outperformance. It expects dental implants to be among the fastest-growing medtech markets through 2030. China price pressure is expected to be offset by volume, restocking and share gains, and the relative valuation sits below historical premiums.

Rolls-Royce (Buy and MP, PT GBP 19, price GBP 12.394): UBS sees the turnaround as incomplete and expects further earnings upgrades. FY26 results are expected around 23 Feb 2027 and may bring higher medium-term cash flow guidance. Civil Aerospace margins are forecast to approach top peers, Defence profitability to exceed most peers, and Power Systems benefits from data centre backup demand.

Siemens (Buy and MP, PT EUR 330, price EUR 265.65): UBS expects strong Q4 results (due 12 Nov) with core orders growth led by Mobility and Smart Infrastructure. Digital Industries depends on an automation recovery. FY27 guidance should support margin expansion as Altair and Dotmatics integration costs fade, and the Healthineers deconsolidation and buybacks may add support.

Barclays (Buy and MP, PT GBP 5.88, price GBP 4.1505): the case rests on investment banking market share, structural hedging earnings, cost actions and capital returns. UBS calls the shares undervalued versus peers, at a 2026 P/E of 6.7 and a 3.41% yield. The price is just above the idea's lower exit level of GBP 4.07.

Rockwool (Buy, PT DKK 265, price DKK 198.8): UBS says Q2 results showed strong volumes and pricing power. Shares fell over 10% on limited estimate changes, which UBS treats as a better entry point. UBS is ahead of consensus for FY26 to FY28, US volumes are surprising positively, July pricing is confirmed, and valuation is near the low end of its historical range.

Oracle (Buy and MP, PT USD 250, new idea 2 Nov 2026): the one-pager's investment-case bullets repeat the Boeing text (USD 750bn backlog, FCF rising from USD 2.2bn to USD 15.1bn) and the performance fields are blank. The company profile bullets are Oracle's, including a plan for 10 gigawatts of data center capacity by fiscal 2028 year-end. Treat the Oracle thesis bullets as a likely template error. The valuation section cites a 28 Oct 2026 UBS note, 'Creditors Applaud, Hence So Do We', and a price target based on an FCF multiple.

Boeing (Buy and MP, PT USD 240, price USD 171.55): UBS cites a nearly USD 750bn backlog, reset expectations and conservative guidance, with free cash flow rising from USD 2.2bn in 2026 to USD 15.1bn by 2030. The 2026 P/E is 152.46 and the yield is 0%. The PT reflects 20.5x EV/EBITDA, and UBS notes a 0% YTD adjusted EBIT margin after development program charges. Risks are weaker air travel, share loss to Airbus or COMAC, supply chain halts and Defense deterioration.

Johnson Controls (Buy and MP, PT USD 190, price USD 149.03): UBS sees double-digit organic revenue growth potential in fiscal 2027, record backlog of about USD 21 billion, and fiscal 2027 EPS about 7% above consensus. It expects incremental margins above the company's long-term framework. The price is near the idea's lower level of USD 138.03.

Expeditors (Buy, PT USD 220, price USD 198.85): airfreight demand from data center and technology customers is described as exceptionally strong. AI tools and a technology restructuring are expected to lift margins, and UBS raised earnings forecasts after a stronger Q2. The idea is up 5.6% since 17 Aug 2026.

Orica (Buy and MP, PT AUD 27, price AUD 22.78): UBS cites tight ammonium nitrate markets, recent acquisitions, a cost reduction program from 2027, and a discount to industrial peers. A fiscal year 2026 result on 12 Nov 2026 is the catalyst, and shares could re-rate if US ammonium nitrate supply concerns ease.

Each idea has upper and lower return limits set by beta: lower 9-12% and upper 12% for beta below 0.8, 12%/16% for beta 0.8 to 1.2, and 15%/20% for beta above 1.2, all from the initiation-day close. If the UBS price target falls below the upper limit, the upper limit is cut to the target and the lower limit is reset to a 1/1.3 risk/reward.

market_movers.rationale: Straumann (STMN SW), incepted 7 Sep 2026 at CHF 93.02, now CHF 97.42 (+4.7%). Implant market growth, margin gains and a valuation below historical premiums support a re-rating.

Rolls-Royce (RR/ LN), CIO Most Preferred, incepted 19 Oct 2026 at GBP 13.316, now GBP 12.394 (-6.9%). UBS expects further earnings upgrades and a possible guidance raise at FY26 results around 23 Feb 2027.

Siemens (SIE GR), CIO Most Preferred, incepted 12 Oct 2026 at EUR 275.75, now EUR 265.65 (-3.7%). Q4 orders led by Smart Infrastructure and Mobility, with the FY27 Digital Industries margin guide key.
Barclays (BARC LN), CIO Most Preferred, incepted 14 Sep 2026 at GBP 4.785, now GBP 4.1505 (-13.3%). UBS cites investment banking strength, cost actions and an undervalued P/E of 6.7.
Rockwool (ROCKB DC), incepted 31 Aug 2026 at DKK 207.2, now DKK 198.8 (-4.1%). UBS says the post-Q2 share drop of over 10% created a stronger entry point and it is ahead of consensus.
Oracle (ORCL US), CIO Most Preferred, new idea incepted 2 Nov 2026. PT is based on an FCF multiple, and the one-pager's thesis bullets appear to be copied from the Boeing page.
Boeing (BA US), CIO Most Preferred, incepted 5 Oct 2026 at USD 192.72, now USD 171.55 (-11.0%). UBS cites a roughly USD 750bn backlog and a free cash flow ramp, with a PT at 20.5x EV/EBITDA.
Johnson Controls (JCI US), CIO Most Preferred, incepted 5 Oct 2026 at USD 156.85, now USD 149.03 (-5.0%). UBS expects fiscal 2027 EPS about 7% above consensus on record backlog.
Expeditors (EXPD US), incepted 17 Aug 2026 at USD 188.27, now USD 198.85 (+5.6%). Airfreight demand from data center and technology customers is strong, and UBS raised EPS forecasts after Q2.
Orica (ORI AU), CIO Most Preferred, incepted 22 Sep 2026 at AUD 22.64, now AUD 22.78 (+0.6%). Ammonium nitrate tightness and a cost program support earnings, with FY26 results on 12 Nov 2026.

sector_views.rationale: UBS expects dental implants to be among the fastest-growing medtech markets through 2030, with value implants and general practitioner adoption supporting procedure growth.
UBS holds Buy ratings on Rolls-Royce and Boeing on backlog, defense wins and civil production increases, though both are below inception price.
UBS holds Barclays as a CIO Most Preferred Buy and cites its own EU banks note, 'we stay overweight'. The case is investment banking revenue, cost actions and capital returns.
Siemens and Johnson Controls are CIO Most Preferred Buys on order and backlog growth and expected margin gains.
Orica is a CIO Most Preferred Buy on tight ammonium nitrate markets, acquisitions and a discount to industrial peers.

earnings_insights: Straumann: Q3 results were scheduled for 28 Oct 2026 and China tender outcomes are due in Q4 2026. UBS says consensus forecasts now look achievable, with modest potential for outperformance.
Rolls-Royce: FY26 results are expected around 23 Feb 2027. UBS sees potential for a guidance upgrade and higher medium-term cash flow guidance. The 2026 P/E is 22.95.

Siemens: Q4 results are due 12 Nov 2026. UBS expects strong core orders growth led by Mobility and Smart Infrastructure and says the FY27 Digital Industries margin guide will be key. The 2026 P/E is 19.44.
Barclays: UBS cites above-budget investment banking revenues in its July note. The 2026 P/E is 6.7 and the 2025 yield is 3.41%.

Rockwool: UBS says Q2 results showed strong volumes and pricing power, with shares down over 10% on limited estimate changes. UBS is ahead of consensus earnings for FY26, FY27 and FY28. The 2026 P/E is 12.77.
Oracle: the 2026 P/E is 14.11 on the page. UBS valuation text cites a price target based on an FCF multiple and a 28 Oct 2026 note.
Boeing: UBS cites a 0% YTD adjusted EBIT margin after development program charges. Free cash flow is forecast at USD 2.2bn in 2026 and USD 15.1bn by 2030, and the 2026 P/E is 152.46.

Johnson Controls: reported record backlog of about USD 21 billion in the prior quarter. UBS forecasts fiscal 2027 EPS about 7% above consensus estimates and double-digit organic revenue growth in fiscal 2027.
Expeditors: UBS raised earnings forecasts after a stronger Q2 (8-K highlights note 11 Aug 2026, 'Raising EPS & PT' note 4 Aug 2026). The 2026 P/E is 22.46.
Orica: fiscal year 2026 result is due 12 Nov 2026. UBS cites a cost reduction program that should support margins from 2027. The 2026 P/E is 17.32.

risk_factors: Barclays at GBP 4.1505 and Johnson Controls at USD 149.03 trade close to their lower exit levels of GBP 4.07 and USD 138.03.
Boeing risks: weaker air travel, share loss to Airbus or COMAC, supply chain issues that could halt deliveries, and Defense business deterioration.
Oracle risks: recent sales reorganization, slipped deals, limited cloud traction and tougher competition.
Siemens: cyclical end markets and a history of downside surprises from exceptional charges.
Barclays: UK macro exposure and investment bank volatility.
Straumann: dental implant cyclicality, product launch issues, discount competition and FX.
Orica: commodity prices, mining customer concentration, ammonium nitrate supply and demand, Burrup AN plant commissioning and weather.
